title: A coordinate ring for an integral projective scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be an integral scheme over a field $k$, equipped with a
closed immersion
$i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$. There is a homogeneous prime
ideal $I\subset k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ such that
$S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/I$ is an integral
standard graded algebra
and $i$ identifies $X$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$.

proof.text:
Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $X$. Its image in projective space
corresponds to a homogeneous prime $I$ not containing the irrelevant
ideal, by [def-pc-proj]. This constructs $I$ without a choice of
equations or any coherent-cohomology theorem. The quotient $S$ is a
domain, its degree-zero part is $k$, and the images of the finitely
many $x_i$ generate it in degree one; these are exactly the conditions
of [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].

We compare the two closed subschemes of $\mathbf P^n_k$ chart by chart. For the standard affine chart $D_+(x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$, $R_i=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_{(x_i)}$ [def-pc-proj], the inverse image $i^{-1}(D_+(x_i))$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i/J_i)$ for an ideal $J_i\subseteq R_i$ by the affine description of closed immersions (Stacks Lemma 01QO) in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If it is nonempty it is an open subscheme of the integral scheme $X$, hence integral, so $R_i/J_i$ is a domain and $J_i$ is the prime of $R_i$ corresponding to its generic point, which is $\eta$. By [def-pc-proj] that prime is $I_{(x_i)}$, the degree-zero part of the graded localization of $I$, and since graded localization is exact, $R_i/I_{(x_i)}=S_{(x_i)}$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. If the inverse image is empty, $\eta\notin D_+(x_i)$, so $x_i\in I$, $S_{(x_i)}=0$ and $J_i=R_i=I_{(x_i)}$. Hence the morphism $\operatorname{Proj}(S)\to\mathbf P^n_k$ induced by $k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\to S$ is, on each chart, $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i/I_{(x_i)})\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ [def-pc-proj], so it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] agrees with that of $i$ on every $D_+(x_i)$, hence everywhere. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] there is a unique isomorphism $X\cong\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ over $\mathbf P^n_k$.
